title: 16.2 RNGD: A 5nm Tensor-Contraction Processor for Power-Efficient Inference on Large Language Models
problem: LLM inference accelerators face a challenge: traditional matrix-multiplication-based architectures fail to fully exploit parallelism and data locality inherent in tensor contractions, limiting throughput and efficiency for LLM workloads.
motivation: LLMs require accelerators combining high memory bandwidth and dense compute with minimal power; traditional matrix multiplication approaches do not naturally map the tensor contraction primitive, leaving parallelism and temporal reuse on the table.
method: RNGD uses tensor contraction as the primitive computational unit instead of matrix multiplication, enabling massive parallelism and time-axis pipelining similar to vector processors; processing elements can be dynamically split into smaller slices with configurable fetch networks for flexible parallelism.
key_novelty: Tensor contraction as computational primitive with dynamic slice-level parallelism and pipelined fetch networks for flexible LLM inference execution.
contributions: Tensor contraction primitive replacing matrix multiplication
Dynamic PE slicing for flexible parallelism
Pipelined fetch network for high data reuse
Deterministic cost models for performance/energy optimization
limitations: Abstract-only; power/performance measurements, comparison with other LLM accelerators, supported LLM architectures/sizes, and latency/throughput not discussed.
primary_theme: Tensor-contraction processor for efficient LLM inference
